answer: Attestation credit is paid per pair, not per signature. The registry counts how often each witness has signed for each author, and the fifth attestation one key gives the same author pays a fraction of the first. A farm of five hundred keys that only ever witness each other saturates those pairs within a day, then signs for nothing. Avoiding the discount means recruiting an outside reader every round, someone whose history is not a vine wrapped around the farm. That inlet stays narrow: internal circulation stops paying, while an honest witness near the zenith of the graph keeps earning.
